source_record.name: ZIP
source_record.standard_status: PKWARE vendor-published APPNOTE 6.3.10, FINAL, revised 2022-11-01; interoperable profiles vary.
source_record.description: Member-oriented container with local records and a central directory.
source_record.storage_relevance: A virtual archive view or import/export layer above an OPFS storage provider; not an independent storage provider.
source_record.read_access: Directory gives member offsets. Stored members permit direct byte ranges; compressed members usually decode from their start. Data descriptors permit streaming creation, but directory-dependent reading needs the tail.
source_record.write_update: Create or rebuild; library-specific append/update must publish a coherent final directory. No filesystem transaction contract.
source_record.metadata: Names, times and host attributes; Unicode, links, ownership and extra fields vary by profile.
source_record.integrity: CRC-32 detects accidental payload corruption; it is not authentication.
source_record.encryption: Distinct profiles: enc-zipcrypto, enc-winzip-aes, enc-pkware-strong and enc-zip-central-directory in the encryption research.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Split/spanned archives are specified; reader and writer support must be checked separately.
implementation_routes: ZIP-specific libraries; libarchive; 7-Zip; separate implementation matrix
constraints: Duplicate names and conflicting local/directory records require a defined policy.
Codec, encryption, metadata and split support are independent capabilities.
source_record.evidence_level: primary specification and/or upstream implementation documentation; integration not tested

source_record.name: 7z
source_record.standard_status: Community/vendor format; upstream 7zFormat.txt is labelled 18.06, with current implementation as additional authority.
source_record.description: Container with coder graphs, compressed headers and optionally solid compression across members.
source_record.storage_relevance: A virtual archive view or import/export layer above an OPFS storage provider; not an independent storage provider.
source_record.read_access: Headers locate streams. A file in a solid block may require decoding earlier data in that block; headers themselves can require decoding or decryption.
source_record.write_update: Create/update with a compatible archiver; changing solid content can require recompression of the affected block and new metadata.
source_record.metadata: Unicode names, directories, timestamps and attributes are represented; complete POSIX ACL/xattr fidelity must be verified per implementation.
source_record.integrity: Header and optional stream CRCs detect corruption; no authentication follows from a CRC.
source_record.encryption: Optional AES and encrypted headers: see enc-7z-aes. CRC integrity is not authenticated encryption.
source_record.split_or_recovery: 7-Zip supports split output; volume handling is an additional reader capability, not parity repair.
implementation_routes: 7-Zip/LZMA SDK; libarchive for its supported subset; separate implementation matrix
constraints: A 7z signature does not identify every codec/filter used.
Bound dictionary memory, decoded header size and solid-block work.
source_record.evidence_level: primary specification and/or upstream implementation documentation; integration not tested

source_record.description: Archive blocks support solid compression, service records, split volumes and optional recovery records.

source_record.metadata: Names, times, attributes, links, Unix owner fields and Windows ACL/alternate-stream service records are available.

source_record.split_or_recovery: Native split volumes and recovery records; successful repair depends on surviving redundancy.
implementation_routes: RAR/WinRAR writer; UnRAR-compatible reader; supported-subset libraries
constraints: The RAR5 container can carry compression revision 1 requiring RAR 7-era decoding.
Archive listing, solid extraction, encryption and recovery are separate support claims.

source_record.name: tar / POSIX ustar
source_record.standard_status: POSIX-defined archive interchange format; historical tar variants remain in use.
source_record.description: Sequential file headers and data records, normally without compression inside the archive.
source_record.storage_relevance: A virtual archive view or import/export layer above an OPFS storage provider; not an independent storage provider.
source_record.read_access: Streamable. An external index can locate uncompressed member data, but ordinary tar carries no global central directory.
source_record.write_update: Sequential creation; append/update tools can add another entry with the same name. Deletion or compaction generally rewrites data.
source_record.metadata: Names, ownership, mode, time, links and device information, with fixed-field limits.
source_record.integrity: Header checksum only; ordinary tar has no payload checksum.
source_record.encryption: No native encryption in ustar; use a separately specified envelope.
source_record.split_or_recovery: GNU and other tools have incompatible multivolume extensions; not a universal ustar property.
implementation_routes: POSIX pax/tar; GNU tar; libarchive; tar-stream-style libraries
constraints: Compressed tar inherits its outer codec's seeking constraints.
Define handling of duplicate paths, links and special files.
source_record.evidence_level: primary specification and/or upstream implementation documentation; integration not tested

source_record.name: POSIX pax extended tar
source_record.standard_status: POSIX extended archive interchange format; vendor extension keywords are separate conventions.
source_record.description: Adds extended key/value records to tar for longer names and richer values.
source_record.storage_relevance: A virtual archive view or import/export layer above an OPFS storage provider; not an independent storage provider.
source_record.read_access: Sequential tar access; global and per-file extended headers affect how following entries are interpreted.
source_record.write_update: Create/rewrite with a declared keyword profile. Unknown metadata must not be silently represented as preserved.

source_record.encryption: External envelope only in the base profile.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Same tool-specific multivolume limits as tar.
implementation_routes: pax; GNU tar; libarchive with explicit extension policy
constraints: pax is both a utility name and an archive format; distinguish them.
Two pax writers can preserve different ACL/xattr conventions.

source_record.name: GNU tar extensions
source_record.standard_status: GNU project conventions, including old GNU and current GNU/pax extensions.
source_record.description: Adds long-name records, sparse representations and incremental-backup records beyond basic ustar.
source_record.storage_relevance: A virtual archive view or import/export layer above an OPFS storage provider; not an independent storage provider.
source_record.read_access: Sequential; extension-aware parsing is necessary before exposing logical files.
source_record.write_update: GNU tar can create/update its supported profiles; some operations require seeking and cannot update compressed archives directly.
source_record.metadata: Long names, sparse maps and incremental directory state are profile-specific; not interchangeable with every pax implementation.
source_record.integrity: Header checksums, with any additional checksum supplied by outer compression.
source_record.encryption: No base tar encryption.
source_record.split_or_recovery: GNU multivolume records exist; not all tar readers implement them.
implementation_routes: GNU tar; explicitly compatible readers
constraints: Do not interpret GNU incremental records as ordinary filenames.
A tar extension handler is a metadata contract, not another storage provider.

source_record.name: Sparse-file archive representations
source_record.standard_status: GNU sparse tar and pax keyword conventions; multiple incompatible historical revisions.
source_record.description: Stores data extents plus logical file length rather than all zero-filled holes.
source_record.storage_relevance: A transformation or preservation behavior above storage; not an independent storage provider.
source_record.read_access: A reader reconstructs requested logical ranges from sparse maps and stored extents.
source_record.write_update: Write a declared sparse revision; editing extents normally rebuilds the archive representation.
source_record.metadata: Hole positions and logical length supplement ordinary tar metadata.
source_record.integrity: Sparse maps do not themselves authenticate data.
source_record.encryption: Inherits surrounding container/envelope.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Not parity; omitted holes are intentional zero regions.
implementation_routes: GNU sparse-aware tar/libarchive; logical range adapter
constraints: GNU sparse 0.0, 0.1 and 1.0 differ.
A reader ignoring the extension can expose an incorrect file.
Charge quotas against logical size as well as stored size.
source_record.evidence_level: primary specification and/or upstream implementation documentation; integration not tested

source_record.name: PAR2 recovery volumes
source_record.standard_status: Community Parity Volume Set Specification v2.0.
source_record.description: Companion recovery packets encode redundancy for a declared set of files.
source_record.storage_relevance: A transformation or preservation behavior above storage; not an independent storage provider.
source_record.read_access: Validate packets and locate intact slices before reconstructing missing/damaged data.
source_record.write_update: Generate or regenerate recovery sets when protected bytes change; not an archive update mechanism.
source_record.metadata: Names and lengths identify protected files; full filesystem metadata is not the purpose.
source_record.integrity: Packet/slice checks use MD5 and CRC-32; Reed-Solomon recovery supplies redundancy, not cryptographic authentication.
source_record.encryption: No encryption; parity may expose information about protected plaintext unless applied to ciphertext.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Recovery is limited by available valid recovery blocks and the damaged/missing data.

source_record.standard_status: Community specification C2SP age v1.1.0; file magic remains age-encryption.org/v1.

source_record.storage_relevance: Optional encrypted-object codec over any byte store; it does not define folders or names.
source_record.read_access: The format supports authenticated chunk seeks after header processing. A seek relative to the end must validate the final chunk. The inspected typage API exposes sequential Web Streams, not a public range reader.
source_record.write_update: The specification forbids modifying the payload without fresh encryption and a fresh nonce.
source_record.metadata: Recipient stanza structure and ciphertext length are observable; external object names are outside this format.
source_record.integrity: Header HMAC and chunk tags detect alterations; completion requires final-chunk validation. Encryption does not identify the sender.
source_record.encryption: ChaCha20-Poly1305 payload in 64 KiB plaintext chunks; recipient algorithms are a separate profile choice.
source_record.split_or_recovery: No parity or key recovery format; preserve a usable identity or passphrase.

source_record.name: OpenPGP RFC 9580 encrypted-message profile
source_record.standard_status: IETF Proposed Standard RFC 9580, July 2024; obsoletes RFC 4880, RFC 5581, and RFC 6637.
source_record.description: Packet-based encryption, signatures, keys, literal data, and optional compression; current SEIPD v2 provides chunked AEAD.
source_record.storage_relevance: Portable encrypted export/import with explicit packet and algorithm negotiation.
source_record.read_access: AEAD chunks can authenticate incrementally. Compression and packet parsing can prevent useful arbitrary plaintext seeks.
source_record.write_update: Treat content changes as a new encrypted message; preserve recipient and signature policy.
source_record.metadata: Encrypted literal metadata is concealed, but document signatures do not bind its filename and timestamp.
source_record.integrity: SEIPD v2 authenticates chunks and final length; signatures separately establish a signer when trusted.
source_record.encryption: OCB is mandatory-to-implement in this AEAD profile; EAX/GCM are additional choices.
source_record.split_or_recovery: No storage parity or automatic key recovery; private-key backups and revocation are separate.
implementation_routes: OpenPGP.js v6 documented RFC 9580 support; AEAD is opt-in through its current configuration
GnuPG compatibility must be tested against the exact emitted profile
constraints: OpenPGP.js v5 draft AEAD and v6 RFC 9580 AEAD are not interchangeable.
Deno support is documented as experimental by OpenPGP.js; this review did not execute it.

source_record.name: OpenPGP RFC 4880-era encrypted message import profiles
source_record.standard_status: Historical Standards Track RFC 4880; superseded by RFC 9580. Retained for explicit legacy interoperability.
source_record.description: Deployed files can contain SEIPD v1 with CFB and a modification-detection code, or older unauthenticated tag-9 encrypted packets.
source_record.storage_relevance: Read/import choices must identify the actual packet profile rather than accept a generic .pgp label.
source_record.read_access: SEIPD v1 integrity is checked at the end; streamed plaintext is provisional until validation completes.
source_record.write_update: New writes should use an explicitly chosen supported current profile; legacy generation is a distinct compatibility decision.
source_record.metadata: Literal metadata and compression have their own rules; outer filenames remain outside the message.
source_record.integrity: The v1 modification-detection code is different from AEAD. Tag 9 provides no cryptographic integrity; RFC 9580 forbids generating it.
source_record.encryption: CFB algorithms and password derivation vary by file and implementation.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Key loss is not repaired by packet recovery or checksums.
implementation_routes: An OpenPGP implementation with narrowly configured legacy import support
constraints: Do not silently disable integrity checks to recover a damaged message.
SHA-1 in an MDC and SHA-1 document signatures are different protocol uses; do not merge their migration rules.

implementation_routes: A compatible GnuPG/LibrePGP implementation with pinned packet behavior
constraints: Tag 20 OCB and RFC 9580 SEIPD-v2/tag-18 AEAD are different wire formats.

source_record.name: CMS EnvelopedData
source_record.standard_status: IETF Standards Track RFC 5652; ASN.1 Cryptographic Message Syntax.
source_record.description: A recipient-aware encrypted-content envelope using key transport, agreement, shared keys, or password mechanisms.
source_record.storage_relevance: Interoperable bulk encrypted objects, certificates, and S/MIME-related exchange.
source_record.read_access: BER indefinite-length encoding can stream data; that does not supply authenticated independent chunks.
source_record.write_update: Produce a new envelope for content changes; key-envelope changes require implementation-specific handling.
source_record.metadata: Recipient information and envelope algorithms are normally visible.
source_record.integrity: EnvelopedData alone does not guarantee content authentication. A CBC envelope is not an AEAD envelope.
source_record.encryption: The selected CMS algorithm profile controls encryption; OpenSSL 3.5 documents AES-256-CBC as its default.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Multiple recipients are alternative key paths; no erasure coding or password recovery.
implementation_routes: OpenSSL cms or a compatible CMS library
An ASN.1/crypto codec integration, not a generic WebCrypto operation
constraints: Use binary handling for arbitrary files; S/MIME text canonicalization can change bytes.
BER streaming output is not necessarily DER.

source_record.split_or_recovery: The inspected profile forbids split ZIP volumes; evidence does not reconstruct missing files.

constraints: A ZIP library is only one component of ASiC support.

source_record.name: Evidence Record Syntax (ERS) and XMLERS
source_record.standard_status: IETF Proposed Standards RFC 4998 (ASN.1 ERS) and RFC 6283 (XMLERS).
source_record.description: Long-term evidence records combine archive timestamps, hash-tree relationships, and renewal history.
source_record.storage_relevance: Optional preservation evidence beside stored objects or embedded in another container.
source_record.read_access: Verification needs the original bytes, evidence path, timestamp trust, and applicable validation information.
source_record.write_update: Renew evidence before cryptographic mechanisms cease to be trustworthy; altered data needs an appropriate new evidence relationship.
source_record.metadata: Evidence and policy/validation material can reveal associations and timing.
source_record.integrity: Designed to preserve evidence of data existence and integrity; it is not a retention service or proof that every stored copy remains available.
source_record.encryption: No standalone payload cipher; encrypted archival data requires its own encryption contract.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Hash trees support grouped evidence, not recovery of missing data.
implementation_routes: An ERS/XMLERS-aware preservation library or service with explicit validation and renewal support
constraints: XMLERS has its own processing rules; it is not merely ASN.1 ERS values pasted into XML.
Keeping the evidence file without operating the renewal/trust lifecycle is insufficient.

source_record.name: rclone crypt file and name format
source_record.standard_status: Documented interoperable project format implemented by the crypt wrapper.
source_record.description: Encrypts objects one-for-one over another rclone remote, with optional name encryption.
source_record.storage_relevance: Composable encrypted-storage behavior over an existing provider.
source_record.read_access: Chunked ciphertext allows offset translation; backend range support and wrapper behavior determine practical reads.
source_record.write_update: Object updates depend on the underlying remote. Changing the configured password does not re-encrypt existing data.
source_record.metadata: Standard name encryption hides names but retains directory structure; obfuscation mode is not strong name encryption. Metadata follows the underlying remote.
source_record.integrity: NaCl SecretBox authenticates content chunks; do not infer a globally authenticated namespace or rollback protection. The documented framing has no authenticated final-length or last-chunk marker, so chunk authentication alone does not establish original file completeness (format-level inference, not an executed test).
source_record.encryption: XSalsa20-Poly1305 content chunks; AES-EME names in standard mode; scrypt-derived keys.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Preserve passwords and optional custom salt. No parity/recovery volume format.
implementation_routes: Existing rclone crypt implementation or compatible wrapper
Separate ciphertext-copy mode
constraints: Filename expansion and provider name limits interact.
A backend checksum of ciphertext is not a plaintext checksum.
Use an independently trusted length, digest, or manifest when complete-file verification is required.

source_record.evidence_level: Primary documentation and published specification review; no executed interoperability or OPFS integration tests.
source_record.catalog_mapping_note: Links preserve related baseline concepts; a detailed format view does not change the original catalog role or imply current OPFS support.
source_record.standard_status: Project-defined. Reviewed stable 1.4.5 format documentation; Borg 2 documentation describes an incompatible repository generation.
source_record.description: Borg 1.x stores keyed objects in a transactional repository using segment records and commit markers; archives reference chunked file content and metadata.
source_record.storage_relevance: A snapshot-aware restore interface above a Borg repository. It cannot be treated as a generic mutable directory of independent user files.
source_record.read_access: Use Borg's archive listing and restore tools. Reading a file requires archive metadata and its referenced chunks; encrypted repositories require the correct key state.
source_record.write_update: Native repository transactions and compaction govern changes. Uncommitted segment operations are ignored; indexes can be rebuilt from committed segments.
source_record.metadata: Archive item records preserve file metadata through the Borg model, subject to the restoration platform.
source_record.integrity: Repository consistency and cryptographic authentication depend on the selected repository mode and client state; a segment index is not a redundant copy of file content.
source_record.encryption: Encryption modes belong to the repository generation. Stable 1.x security documentation relies on trusted persistent client state and restricts independent multi-client mutation assumptions.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Segments and chunks are internal layout units. Index reconstruction cannot recover lost encrypted chunks without another copy.
implementation_routes: Native Borg CLI and its supported remote repository mode; export an archive view through a separately controlled integration.
constraints: Do not apply Borg 1.x crypto, format, or CLI claims to Borg 2.
Borg 2 migration requires a new repository and the documented transfer path; it is not an in-place parser upgrade.
No browser or Deno repository implementation was validated.

source_record.name: Duplicacy repository
source_record.evidence_level: Primary documentation and published specification review; no executed interoperability or OPFS integration tests.
source_record.catalog_mapping_note: Links preserve related baseline concepts; a detailed format view does not change the original catalog role or imply current OPFS support.
source_record.standard_status: Project-defined snapshot/chunk format and coordination algorithm.
source_record.description: Snapshots reference content-defined chunks; metadata sequences are chunked too. A chunk can contain portions of adjacent source files.
source_record.storage_relevance: A deduplicated backup view over configured storage, with repository operations that exceed an ordinary archive reader's contract.
source_record.read_access: Native list, restore, and check operations resolve snapshot sequences and chunk offsets. Restore can read a fossil when its normal chunk object is absent.
source_record.write_update: Backups publish chunks and snapshots. Garbage collection first marks unreferenced chunks as fossils, then removes them only after coordination conditions are met.
source_record.metadata: Snapshot records include revision, times, file sequence, chunk sequence, and lengths; metadata is part of the deduplicated graph.
source_record.integrity: Content hashing identifies chunks; encrypted configurations add authenticated encryption. Optional erasure coding is a separate configured feature.
source_record.encryption: Optional encrypted repositories use AES-GCM for chunk and snapshot content; random keys are stored in an encrypted configuration protected by a password-derived master key.
source_record.split_or_recovery: The project's erasure-coding feature can recover corruption within a chunk up to configured parity limits; its maintainer explicitly excludes recovery of an entirely missing chunk.
implementation_routes: Official native Go CLI or its GUI; use the project's storage and snapshot operations.
constraints: Retain the fossil collection protocol when integrating writes or deletes.
Parity does not replace another copy of a missing chunk or recover a lost password.
Official CLI licensing distinguishes personal/trial and commercial backup use; verify applicable terms before redistribution or deployment.

source_record.description: File-list volumes identify versions, block volumes hold payload chunks, and index volumes accelerate block lookup.
source_record.storage_relevance: A versioned backup set above local or remote storage. Individual ZIP-like volumes are components, not self-contained restores.
source_record.read_access: Native restore resolves file lists and block locations through a local or rebuilt database. Without indexes it may need to inspect block volumes.
source_record.write_update: Use native backup, delete, compact, and repair operations to coordinate remote volumes and local state.

source_record.encryption: Documented options include AES Crypt-compatible volume encryption and GPG through an external executable. Encrypted volumes require their credentials before archive inspection.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Current documentation describes optional PAR2 companions for dblock and dlist files, not dindex files. Recovery depends on available parity and damage extent.
implementation_routes: Official Duplicati CLI or service; dedicated decrypt/repair tools support controlled recovery workflows.
constraints: Do not modify remote volume files independently of Duplicati's repository operations.

source_record.standard_status: Service-specific client format and protocol; this row describes archive semantics, while the catalog's tarsnap ID describes the service.
source_record.description: The client builds tar-derived archive metadata, splits file data into content-dependent chunks, and deduplicates, compresses, and encrypts before upload.
source_record.storage_relevance: An encrypted archive view mediated by Tarsnap's client and service, not a portable unencrypted tar object on an arbitrary backend.
source_record.read_access: Use the native client with authorized keys to enumerate archives and restore referenced chunks.

source_record.integrity: The documented design uses authenticated cryptographic structures and signed Merkle-tree hashes; transport availability is separate.
source_record.encryption: Per-archive AES-256 keys are wrapped by RSA keys. Losing the necessary keys makes encrypted archive data unrecoverable.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Shared chunks reduce duplication. No independent parity or offline self-contained archive-recovery contract was established in this review.
implementation_routes: Official Tarsnap native client; expose its restore/export operations through a separate process or service integration.
constraints: The existing tarsnap backend classification is unchanged; this is a deeper format-related view.
Do not advertise generic S3 access, browser support, or direct mutation of server objects from these documents.

source_record.name: Duplicity full and incremental backup chains
source_record.evidence_level: Primary documentation and published specification review; no executed interoperability or OPFS integration tests.
source_record.catalog_mapping_note: Links preserve related baseline concepts; a detailed format view does not change the original catalog role or imply current OPFS support.
source_record.standard_status: Project-defined GNU tar-based data/signature volumes and manifests; current primary format and CLI documentation reviewed.
source_record.description: A full backup supplies base files; later sets contain new files, librsync binary deltas, and deletion markers.
source_record.storage_relevance: A time-selectable restore view over coordinated backup volumes, rather than a collection of independent ordinary tar archives.
source_record.read_access: Use native time/path selection. Restoring a later state applies the required base and deltas in order; manifests identify needed volumes.
source_record.write_update: Native full and incremental operations create backup sets. Current signature data is needed to append an incremental backup; retain complete dependency chains during cleanup.
source_record.metadata: GNU tar entries preserve source attributes. Manifests describe volume ranges and hashes; signature archives contain librsync change-detection data.
source_record.integrity: Native verify downloads data and tests restore/hash results. A successful list from signatures does not establish that payload volumes still exist or are intact.
source_record.encryption: GnuPG supports symmetric encryption or encryption to public keys, with optional signing; no-encryption is also an explicit mode.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Large snapshots/deltas can span volumes. Splitting adds no parity; deleting the necessary full set can make later increments unusable.
implementation_routes: Official Duplicity CLI over its documented backend implementations; a native export/restore integration is distinct from a tar parser.
constraints: A librsync signature is change-detection data, not a cryptographic signer identity.
Signature files are not required for restore, but data volumes and restore manifests are; preserve their separate roles.
The documented Unix metadata model excludes hard-link preservation.
Browser and direct OPFS execution were not established.

constraints: Confine every manifest and fetch target to the bag root.

source_record.standard_status: Community specification; latest published redirect resolves to version 1.1, updated 7 November 2024.
source_record.description: Version directories and inventories map logical object states to immutable content files.
source_record.storage_relevance: A preservation object and version view over hierarchical filesystems or object-store namespaces.
source_record.read_access: Resolve the selected version's inventory state to content paths; each version describes a complete logical object even when bytes are reused.
source_record.write_update: Assemble a new version, publish its content, and update the head inventory with recoverable coordination. The specification defines objects at rest; implementation notes discuss operations.

source_record.split_or_recovery: Forward-delta versions reuse bytes. Checksums identify corruption; they do not create redundant repair data.
implementation_routes: A specification-conforming object/inventory adapter over existing OPFS filesystem primitives; no existing OPFS OCFL implementation is claimed.
constraints: Do not equate object-store copy/delete with atomic filesystem rename.
The implementation notes' staged publication and transaction identifiers need a backend-specific failure-recovery design.
Retain logical paths and immutable version content rather than exposing raw inventory edits as ordinary file mutations.

source_record.evidence_level: Primary documentation and published specification review; no executed interoperability or OPFS integration tests.
source_record.catalog_mapping_note: Links preserve related baseline concepts; a detailed format view does not change the original catalog role or imply current OPFS support.
source_record.standard_status: WARC 1.1 corresponds to ISO 28500:2017; primary public specification hosted by IIPC.
source_record.description: A stream of typed records that preserves captured responses, requests, metadata, and references to earlier payloads.
source_record.storage_relevance: Provides addressable capture records and replay data, not merely an opaque document format.
source_record.read_access: Sequential record parsing is native to the layout. External indexes plus independently gzip-compressed records permit selected range reads.
source_record.write_update: Append/write records and regenerate affected indexes. A capture or replay engine must interpret record relationships.
source_record.metadata: Record identifiers, dates, target URIs, HTTP information, and warcinfo/metadata records retain capture context.
source_record.integrity: Block and payload digest headers support verification when present and checked; revisit records can depend on payload data stored elsewhere.
source_record.encryption: No general encryption or private-name layer is defined by the core WARC record format.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Segmentation can divide large records; revisit deduplication is not redundancy. An incomplete capture may not contain all resources required for replay.
implementation_routes: webrecorder/warcio reads WARC and legacy ARC streams and writes WARC; its default output is WARC 1.0 unless 1.1 is requested.
constraints: Record-level gzip is required for efficient indexed compressed access; one whole-file gzip stream has different seek costs.
Archived web content remains untrusted active content during replay.
ARC reading does not imply ARC writing in the cited implementation.

source_record.description: A ZIP/ZIP64 package combines WARC data, capture indexes, page metadata, and resource manifests for portable replay.
source_record.storage_relevance: Adds a searchable capture view with ranged retrieval above ZIP and WARC.
source_record.read_access: Use the ZIP directory and CDXJ indexes to locate WARC record ranges without downloading the entire collection when the source supports the required access.
source_record.write_update: Assemble archives and indexes with matching manifests; content changes require corresponding index and checksum updates.
source_record.metadata: datapackage.json, page lists, and index entries describe captures and contained resources.

implementation_routes: Webrecorder py-wacz creates and validates packages; its documentation links ReplayWeb.page for replay and authsign for optional signatures.
constraints: Already compressed WARC and index members must be stored without an additional ZIP compression layer where the specification requires range access.
A remote browser viewer needs suitable HTTP range and cross-origin response support.
Archive identity and signer trust require validation beyond a successful ZIP listing.

source_record.evidence_level: Primary documentation and published specification review; no executed interoperability or OPFS integration tests.
source_record.catalog_mapping_note: Links preserve related baseline concepts; a detailed format view does not change the original catalog role or imply current OPFS support.
source_record.standard_status: Library of Congress-maintained XML standard. METS 2 was released 3 March 2025; METS 1 remains a separate compatibility target.
source_record.description: XML descriptions connect digital-object files with descriptive, administrative, and structural metadata.
source_record.storage_relevance: Provides package navigation and file references, not storage allocation or a byte-serving protocol.
source_record.read_access: Parse the declared METS generation/profile and resolve file references under a restricted policy.
source_record.write_update: Generate XML consistent with the target profile and update references when package members change.
source_record.metadata: Structure maps and associated metadata connect logical objects to stored files.
source_record.integrity: Checksums and identifiers are declarations that a package validator can verify; they do not perform verification automatically.
source_record.encryption: No built-in payload encryption, password derivation, or key lifecycle.
source_record.split_or_recovery: References can connect distributed files; they are not replicas or erasure-code fragments.
implementation_routes: Version-aware XML schema/profile validation alongside package file operations.
constraints: METS 2 is a revised schema, not an automatic drop-in replacement for METS 1 profiles.
Do not enable arbitrary external XML entities or unrestricted referenced-resource fetches.

source_record.name: OCI image layout and filesystem layers
source_record.evidence_level: Primary documentation and published specification review; no executed interoperability or OPFS integration tests.
source_record.catalog_mapping_note: Links preserve related baseline concepts; a detailed format view does not change the original catalog role or imply current OPFS support.
source_record.standard_status: Open Container Initiative image specification; image-layout and filesystem-layer contracts are distinct from the Distribution API.
source_record.description: A directory layout stores opaque content-addressed blobs, a layout version, and an image index; manifests can reference filesystem-layer changesets.
source_record.storage_relevance: A digest-indexed package view, with optional reconstruction of layered filesystem content.
source_record.read_access: Resolve index and manifest descriptors, verify blobs, and apply layers in order when exposing a filesystem view.
source_record.write_update: Create new blobs and manifests, then publish references consistently. A tar export is one transport representation of the layout.
source_record.metadata: Descriptors, media types, image configuration, and indexes describe relationships and platform variants.
source_record.integrity: Digest-addressed blobs allow integrity checking; descriptor validation must precede trusting referenced bytes.
source_record.encryption: The core image layout does not establish a general encrypted-archive contract.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Layers share content but are not redundancy. Missing referenced layers can prevent reconstruction.
implementation_routes: A layout reader over OPFS files plus a separate layer interpreter; a generic tar extractor alone is insufficient.
constraints: Whiteout/deletion semantics and link handling must follow the layer specification.
Do not equate OCI image storage with starting a container or with a registry backend implementation.
Preserve unknown layout files as permitted by the specification.

source_record.name: IPLD CAR version 1
source_record.evidence_level: Primary documentation and published specification review; no executed interoperability or OPFS integration tests.
source_record.catalog_mapping_note: Links preserve related baseline concepts; a detailed format view does not change the original catalog role or imply current OPFS support.
source_record.standard_status: IPLD community transport specification.
source_record.description: A header identifies roots, followed by length-delimited CID-and-block sections.
source_record.storage_relevance: An archive/blockstore interchange view for content-addressed data, independent of a storage network.
source_record.read_access: Sequential parsing is built in. A separately created CID-to-offset index can support selected block reads.
source_record.write_update: Write block sections and an appropriate header using a CAR writer; preserve the chosen content graph contract.
source_record.metadata: Root CIDs and block codecs identify content, but do not supply ordinary file names or a filesystem model on their own.
source_record.integrity: Verify each block against its CID using an allowed hash function. Root CIDs alone do not describe all archive contents or prove complete DAG inclusion.
source_record.encryption: No encryption, access control, or retention guarantee is supplied by CAR.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Multiple blocks are a layout, not parity. DAG completeness and redundant copies require separate checks/policies.
implementation_routes: @ipld/car JavaScript reader/writer and ipld/go-car native library; choose streaming/indexed APIs appropriate to the input.
constraints: @ipld/car explicitly does not verify block bytes against CIDs automatically on read.
The format does not require that the roots describe complete DAGs or all contained blocks.
Set block-length, total-byte, multihash, and codec policies before processing untrusted data.

source_record.name: IPLD CAR version 2
source_record.evidence_level: Primary documentation and published specification review; no executed interoperability or OPFS integration tests.
source_record.catalog_mapping_note: Links preserve related baseline concepts; a detailed format view does not change the original catalog role or imply current OPFS support.
source_record.standard_status: IPLD community specification marked Draft; deployed implementations exist.
source_record.description: Adds a fixed header with data offsets and sizes, optional padding, and an optional index after the CARv1 payload.
source_record.storage_relevance: Enables an indexed blockstore/archive view while retaining an extractable CARv1 payload.
source_record.read_access: The optional index maps hash digests to offsets relative to the nested CARv1 payload; enforce that payload's declared extent.
source_record.write_update: Keep header offsets, payload size, and index consistent through a CARv2-aware writer.
source_record.metadata: Header characteristics and an index codec supplement CARv1 metadata.
source_record.integrity: An index does not authenticate blocks or prove complete DAG availability.
source_record.encryption: No encryption or retention service.
source_record.split_or_recovery: Fully-indexed describes section coverage, not parity or DAG completeness.
implementation_routes: ipld/go-car/v2 provides the version-specific native implementation route; verify a chosen JavaScript library's CARv2 contract rather than inferring it from CARv1 support.
constraints: An index may be absent.
Index offsets use the nested payload's origin.
Validate sizes and actual reads before allocation.
